newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Britain not to meddle in HK assembly.
newsitem.headline: China tells Britain not to meddle in HK assembly.

text.p: China warned Britain on Tuesday that any attempt to challenge China in the World Court on the legality of a new Chinese-sanctioned provisional legislature for Hong Kong would damage Sino-British ties.
"If Britain does this, this will damage Sino-Birtish relations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
"If the British act wilfully, create troubles and do not cooperate with the Chinese side, then Sino-British relations will be damaged," Shen said when asked about the British proposal.

British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind last Friday challenged China to let the World Court rule on the legality of the new legislature, selected by a Chinese-appointed committee at the weekend to replace the elected Legislative Council when Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
"Playing the international card is useless," Shen said.
"To cooperate with China is of benefit to Britain, otherwise it will not be beneficial," he said. "This will interfere in China's internal affairs."
